title: Gold below $4,000/oz attracts ETF inflows, led by US - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Investments were $1.66 billion and redemptions $0.99 billion, leaving the inflows net positive at $672.8 million. | Photo Credit: KSL

Inflows into physically backed gold exchange-traded funds (ETFs) were net positive last week, as investors found the yellow metal’s price below $4,000 an ounce attractive.

Data from the World Gold Council (WGC) showed that in the week ending November 13, investments were $1.66 billion and redemptions $0.99 billion, leaving the inflows net positive at $672.8 million.

UK, Japanese and Chinese investors continued to redeem, while US investors were positive. Investors in the UK encashed $131 million, while Chinese investors encashed $23 million. Japanese investors’ redemptions were the highest at $194 million.

In contrast, inflows in the US were $766 million, and in Germany and Switzerland, they were $95 million and $73.8 million, respectively. French and South African investments, too, were net positive. Data on Indian ETF investments were unavailable.

“Central banks, led by China, kept buying, and ETF holdings stayed high, while speculators cut longs,” said Prithviraj Kothari, Managing Director at RiddiSiddhi Bullions Ltd., President of India Bullion and Jewellers Association Ltd.

Renisha Chainani, Chief Research Officer at Augmont, said gold is under pressure for two different reasons. “One is that confidence in the dollar has returned. The other is forced selling: investors facing margin calls and funding pressure sell what is liquid, gold included, to raise dollars,” she said, explaining the precious metal dropping below $4,000 an ounce.

Gold swaps at the Bank for International Settlements rose from about 141 tonnes in August to 218 tonnes by October, which would suggest gold is being used as collateral to raise dollars, said Chainani.

On Monday, gold was down a tad from the weekend to $3,870 an ounce at 1900 hours IST. The yellow metal has lost over 30 per cent after it soared to a record high of $5,608.

Year-to-date, investments in gold ETFs were $138.85 billion and redemptions $98.04 billion, leaving inflows net positive at $40.8 billion.

Chinese holdings in gold ETFs are the highest at $10.21 billion, followed by UK investors at $9.98 billion. Indian investments are over $5 billion, while US inflows are net positive at $4.26 billion.

Switzerland ($3.68 billion), Germany ($2.65 billion), France ($1.11 billion), and the Hong Kong State Administered Region ($1.03 billion) are other nations where investments continue to be net positive.

Darshan Desai, CEO of Aspect Bullion & Refinery, said gold is expected to remain volatile, driven by US economic data, Federal Reserve commentary, geopolitical developments and currency movements. “We expect consolidation and cautious buying to define the near-term market trend,” he said.

Chainani said, "We would stay cautious in the near term and treat rallies towards $4,000 as selling opportunities until the Fed outlook settles.”

Gold has plunged in recent weeks on a stronger dollar and higher Treasury yields. These have been aided by hopes of the US Fed tightening its monetary policy and raising interest rates in view of surging inflation.

Gold rallied between 2024 and January 2026 on hopes of US Fed rate cuts, geopolitical tensions and the trade war between the US and its other global partners.
